newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra to sell ADI in a yr or so - McLachlan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra to sell ADI in a yr or so - McLachlan.

text.p: The Australian government said on Thursday that its arms maker and property developer ADI Ltd was fit for sale to the private sector, a transaction that could occur this year or next.
"I imagine that (the sale) will be in the next year or so," Defence Minister Ian McLachlan told parliament.
Sources familiar with ADI's accounts estimated two years ago that the company was worth about A$500 million.
McLachlan said buyers had shown interest.

"There is now widespread recognition within the industry of the improved operating performance of the company and considerable interest has developed, and I might say they (ADI) have done very well," McLachlan said.
"It's now clear that the company is successfully transforming itself into a viable commercial entity and accordingly we will be looking at the optimum time for its transition into private hands."
The Australian subsidiary of British Aerospace Plc showed interest in ADI on Tuesday.
Asked whether it might buy ADI, a spokeswoman for British Aerospace Australia said her company was very keen to participate in the consolidation of the local defence industry.
ADI, formerly Australian Defence Industries, is itself a consolidation of the Australian Defence Department's manufacturing facilities.
It makes ammunition, firearms, minehunters and other defence equipment.
Over the past few years the company has closed old factories and a firing range, making the sites available for sale.
The former firing range, surrounded by Sydney suburbs, is becoming a very large housing development.
But analysts say the company's manufacturing operation is a difficult asset to sell because the Australian Defence Department is a near monopoly customer.
A spokesman for McLachlan said on Tuesday that sale of ADI was not a short-term priority.
